entries.title: Visitors explore the Obama Presidential Center museum on opening day
entries.summary: <p>Some were wowed by the feeling of sitting behind the desk in the Oval Office replica.</p><p>One visitor thought of all the people who helped build the place — because she's married to one of them.</p><p>And still others were just overwhelmed by remembering what the election of the first Black president meant to them, and to the country,</p><p>That's just a few of the thoughts from the visitors lucky enough to score much-coveted tickets to the museum of the Obama Presidential Center on its grand opening.</p><p>They were among thousands of visitors from across the country who packed nearly every corner of the campus in Jackson Park Friday to celebrate a place and a president on Juneteenth.</p><h3>Delores Mcclendon, 45, Englewood</h3><p>Delores Mcclendon spent hours touring the museum, but one installation in particular gave her the chance to relive one of the most significant moments not only of her own life, but for many others as well.</p><p>Mcclendon said the exhibit that stood out most was a video replaying the day former President Barack Obama won the 2008 presidential election.</p><p>“I remember that night, sitting there watching with my family,” said Mcclendon. “We were all shedding tears as he was getting closer and closer to winning. We were rejoicing.”</p><p>But before he became president, Obama was her neighbor, she said.</p><p>“He's from Chicago and that's the most exciting thing to me,” said Mcclendon. “To know that somebody that came up in the same community, and made it this far, made such a great impact in our nation, is incredible.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" </div><p></p><h3>Janice Murdock, 62, Auburn Gresham </h3><h3></h3><p>As Janice Murdock walked through the replica of the Oval Office, she said she couldn’t help but reflect on how far Black Americans have come.</p><p>“It’s overwhelming,” she said. “To be able to sit in the seat that [Barack Obama] sat in is awe-inspiring.”</p><p>The moment felt even more meaningful as opening day coincided with Juneteenth, a holiday commemorating emancipation, and one giving Black Americans an opportunity to celebrate freedom.</p><p>Murdock said the museum is a reflection of everything Obama was able to accomplish.</p><p>“He continues to give us so much hope,” said Murdock. “He set a standard that we so long looked for.”</p><h3>Verena Jimenez, 33, West Lawn</h3><h3></h3><p>Verena Jimenez said she enjoyed walking through the museum and taking in the artwork, but what made the experience especially meaningful was knowing her husband played a role in building a piece of history.</p><p> Victor Guevara, was among the construction workers who helped build the Obama Presidential Center. His name is engraved on the Worker Appreciation Wall, a permanent installation honoring the thousands of people who worked on the project.</p><p>Guevara smiled shyly as his wife spoke about his accomplishment.</p><p>“It’s been a great experience,” he said.</p><p>He and his wife brought their children to the museum on opening day, where Jimenez said she was grateful to get a glimpse at Obama’s legacy.</p><p>“He is one of the greatest presidents this country has ever seen,” she said. “He’s impacted our family and thousands of other people.”</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: White Sox say longtime shortstop Jacob Gonzalez catching on fast at first
entries.summary: <p>DETROIT — What makes the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a>’ playoff push unique is the fact that they’re doing it with players lacking major-league experience. And some of them aren’t just lacking that — they’re lacking it at the position they’re playing.</p><p>Case in point: Jacob Gonzalez.</p><p>The Sox called up Gonzalez with the intention of playing him at first base after Munetaka Murakami strained his right hamstring May 29, even though Gonzalez, primarily a shortstop, had started only five games there in his college and minor-league careers. He forced his way onto the roster with 19 home runs in 52 games at Triple-A Charlotte this season.</p><p>“He’s here to play first base for us,” Venable said days after Gonzalez’s call-up. “We’re going to support him.”</p><p>That they are.</p><p>“That’s where it gets lost with guys that play in the middle or even just on the left side of the infield,” Sox third-base and infield coach Justin Jirschele told the Sun-Times. “Go over to first base, and it’ll be easy. But it’s not. There’s a lot of nuance to it.”</p><p>Though Gonzalez has had a couple of mental miscues, he’s handling the physical aspects of the position well. In fact, according to the website The Fielding Bible, Gonzalez has a defensive runs saved of plus-two, meaning he’s above average (average is zero).</p><p>“The amount of runs he’s saved, the amount of double plays he’s started, the amount of picks he’s had in the dirt, overall, he’s been really, really good,” Jirschele said. “Especially for how new he is there.</p><p>“He’s working on his backhand. And you have to remember, he’s used to using a [smaller] glove, and now it’s damn near double. Yeah, it’s a bigger glove to catch throws, but fielding ground balls, it’s a much different feel.”</p><p>His two blunders were costly. On June 2 against the Twins, he moved to field a ball bunted back to pitcher Davis Martin, putting him out of position to take Martin’s throw. On Tuesday against the Yankees, he thought a ball was headed to the outfield, so he moved toward the mound to be the cut-off man. When second baseman Chase Meidroth fielded it, he had no one to throw to.</p><p>Gonzalez’s lesson: Go to the base first.</p><p>“The game’s always the best teacher for all of us,” Jirschele said. “We’re going to make mistakes; we learn from them. That’s exactly what I told him [Wednesday]. ‘I bet you that doesn’t happen again because you’re going to learn from that.’ ”</p><p>Where Gonzalez’s experience as a shortstop comes in handy is when he’s manning the right side of the infield seemingly alone with a right-handed hitter at the plate.</p><p>“If you watch where he’s playing and how aggressive he is on right-handed hitters, he’s almost halfway to second base,” Jirschele said. “But he’s comfortable enough to play there. It doesn’t happen a ton, but just optically, it takes away righties from feeling comfortable. It speaks volumes to how much he’s grown there in such a short period of time.”</p><p>Though Gonzalez has started just once this week, it has nothing to do with his play at first and everything to do with matchups. The Sox have faced three lefties, putting the left-handed-hitting Gonzalez on the bench. He’ll be in the lineup Saturday, when the Tigers start right-hander Troy Melton. That’s another issue for Gonzalez, who’s hitless in his last seven games.</p><p>But in the field, maybe we’ll see something else Gonzalez has learned. This much is certain: The Sox like what they’re seeing.</p><p>“All in all, it’s just a new position that he’s extremely young in,” Jirschele said. “He’s young in general, but extremely young at first base. entries.title: Cubs' offense erupts for 16 runs, including seven-run first inning
entries.summary: <p>The Cubs would like to believe they're getting back to being their old, offensive selves.</p><p> </p><p>They hit the Toronto Blue Jays and veteran starter Kevin Gausman with seven runs in the first inning on Friday at Wrigley Field and just kept pouring it on in a 16-2 win.</p><p> </p><p>Carson Kelly provided the big blow in the early outburst —  his second career grand slam — off Gausman’s first pitch to him, a down-the-middle slider. </p><p> </p><p>Seiya Suzuki’s double to the right field corner had already given the North Siders a 2-0 lead. Then Kelly’s drive sailed 428-feet, landed just under the left-field video board and made it it 6-0.</p><p> </p><p>Add three more singles and the Cubs tied their season-high with seven runs in a frame.  </p><p></p><p>The rally was enough for the Cubs to win a second straight game and for the sixth time in eight.  Starter Ben Brown went on cruise control, throwing 51 of 72 pitches for strikes through six innings, walking none. The right-hander allowed just two runs on four hits to win his third straight decision</p><p> </p><p>It also was the third time the North Siders scored three runs in inning this season.  It also was the second time in<i> two games</i>, following a seven-run second inning in an 8-6 win at Colorado on Wednesday.</p><p> </p><p>“Right from the get-go, guys put pressure on them," said Kelly, who finished with career-high six RBIs. "It was get it to the next guy, continued to get it to the next guy. It was awesome.”</p><p> </p><p>The Cubs finished with 18 hits against defending the AL champs in this one. This is a Cubs squad that piled up runs early in the season during two 10-game winning streaks that book-ended a 20-3 run.</p><p> </p><p>Gausman issued four walks, along with yielding five hits in the first to set up the Cubs big inning as they sent 12 men to the plate. Gausman said he was wilder than usual – he entered having issued just 16 passes in 87 innings </p><p></p><p>“I wish I could point to something,” Gausman said. "The walks more than anything. That’s not normally me.”</p><p> </p><p>Meanwhile,the The Cubs were prudent.</p><p> </p><p>We did a good job against him to get that rally moving,” manager Craig Counsell said. "Obviously we got a huge hit from Carson, but we made (Gausman) come in the zone and laid off the splitter down and off the slider away to the righties and that’s important."</p><p> </p><p>Lead-off man Pete Crow-Armstrong continued to sizzle at the plate. The dynamic center fielder had three singles, an RBI and walked twice to extend his career-high on-base streak to 22 games, He’s batting .409 during the stretch.</p><p> </p><p>The free-swinging slugger is up to 27 walks in 76 games his season. He had 29 for all for 2025.</p><p> </p><p>“Today was the definition of who we are,” Crow-Armstrong said. "Drawing walks agaist a guys who doesn’t walk many, mixed with hits and homers.. or a homer. </p><p> </p><p>"That’s exactly who we are. We put ourselves in really good opportunities today to hit with guys guys on.  Contrary to recently, we made the most of those opportunities really well. Today was just a really good example of who this team is."</p><p></p><p>The Cubs accepted a total of 11 walks in this one from seven pitchers, including Toronto outfielder Miles Straw who mopped up for the final four outs.</p><p></p><p>The Cubs added four more runs in the sixth and five in the seventh. Seiya Suzuki and Nico Hoerner each had a double among three hits.</p><p> </p><p>The biggest, most emotional knock was a triple from Justin Dean, a 29-year-old who had been called up from Triple-A Iowa before the game and replaced Crow-Armstrong in center in the seventh.  The journeyman’s first major league hit drove in three runs.</p><p> </p><p>Dean sliced a drive of right-handed submariner Tyler Rogers beyond Jesus Sanchez to the right field corrner, then raced to third.  Dean appeared in 18 games with the Dodgers last season, but had only two at-bats has he was used in pinch-hitting and defensive replacement roles after a mix of 10 seasons in the minors, Mexico and college ball.<br></p>

entries.title: Man fatally shot in West Pullman, another injured
entries.summary: <p>A 29-year-old man was shot in West Pullman Friday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>He was standing near the sidewalk in the 11900 block of South Michigan Avenue at 5:14 p.m. when he was shot multiple times by someone in an SUV, police said. He was taken to Roseland Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.</p><p>A 70-year-old man standing near the sidewalk was also shot in the leg. He was taken to Christ Hospital and was listed in stable condition.<br></p>

entries.title: Mike Vasil gets under Tarik Skubal's skin in White Sox' loss to Tigers
entries.summary: <p>DETROIT — It’s not often that the first person reporters approach in the clubhouse after a game is an injured player who’s out for the season.</p><p>But that was the case Friday at Comerica Park, where the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> lost to the Tigers 4-3 in a snippy and snappy game.</p><p>With the bases loaded and the score tied at 2 in the top of the fifth, Tigers ace <b>Tarik Skubal</b> struck out <b>Colson Montgomery</b> with the bases loaded to end the inning. As he walked off the field, Skubal shouted and gestured toward the Sox’ dugout, apparently perturbed by injured pitcher <b>Mike Vasil’s</b> high jinks with his ‘‘magical’’ wand.</p><p>‘‘It was good, clean fun,’’ said Vasil, who’s recovering from Tommy John surgery. ‘‘I was just up there on the top step, helping the team out, cheering them on. Next thing I know, I’m getting reamed out.</p><p>‘‘There were some pretty choice words, and then I shared back some choice words. It was good stuff.’’</p><p>The umpires gathered to discuss the matter, but nothing came of it.</p><p>Sox manager <b>Will Venable</b> wondered whether the Tigers were accusing the Sox of stealing signs.</p><p>With the wand?</p><p>‘‘I have no idea,’’ Venable said. ‘‘Everything that we do on our bench is inward; it’s aboveboard. We had two umpires coming over and talking to us and no one talking to their side. It was their guy on the mound that was yelling and causing a scene. We were just trying to explain that there was nothing going on and didn’t really know what the problem was.’’</p><p>Vasil said Skubal hadn’t said anything to the Sox until then.</p><p>‘‘We started to get on base, and people get paranoid,’’ he said.</p><p>The bigger issue was that the Sox scored only one run in the inning and left the bases loaded. Though <b>Junior Perez</b> followed his first major-league hit with his first big-league home run in the sixth to give the Sox a 3-2 lead, it was short-lived.</p><p>In the bottom of the inning, <b>Kerry Carpenter</b> blooped a two-out, two-run double in front of a charging <b>Tristan Peters</b> in center field against <b>Erick Fedde</b>, who otherwise had a fine outing.</p><p>‘‘Big spot with two guys on, I felt like I made the pitch I wanted to,’’ said Fedde, who threw a cutter. ‘‘It was a good piece of hitting.’’</p><h3>Notes</h3><p>Venable batted <b>Miguel Vargas</b> first in the order, only the fifth time in Vargas’ career he batted leadoff.</p><p>“Just wanted to mix it up and give Miguel the opportunity to get as many at-bats as possible against Skubal,” Venable said. “He’s our best hitter against left-handed pitching.”</p><p>Vargas went 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.</p><p>• Catcher <b>Kyle Tee</b>l (hamstring, knee) had four hits in five at-bats with two runs scored and two RBI in his rehab outing Friday at Triple-A Charlotte. He’s scheduled to play another nine innings Saturday, then be evaluated for a potential return.</p><p>• Left-hander <b>Noah Schultz</b> (knee) is scheduled to throw 50 to 60 pitches (about three entries.title: The Cubs' Justin Dean's first major-league hit was a long time coming
entries.summary: <p>Cubs manager <b>Craig Counsell</b> said speedy outfielder<b> Justin Dean</b> would be used in pinch-running and defensive-replacement roles after his call-up from Triple-A Iowa before Friday’s 16-2 victory against the Blue Jays.</p><p>The 29-year-old Dean replaced hot-hitting <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b> in center in the seventh inning after the Cubs had taken an 11-2 lead. In the bottom of the frame, Dean tripled with the bases loaded for his first major-league hit.</p><p>Dean, from Maudlin, South Carolina, had toiled in the minors and Mexico for 10 seasons before appearing in 18 regular-season games with the Dodgers last season. But he had only two at-bats and plate appearances as he was relegated to a specialized role in Los Angeles.</p><p>Dean went on to appear in 13 postseason games with the World Series champs but had no plate appearances, even if he did score as a pinch runner.</p><p>In his first at-bat with the Cubs, the right-handed batting Dean sliced a center-cut sinker from right-handed submariner <b>Tyler Rogers</b> beyond right fielder <b>Jesus Sanchez</b> and into the corner. Dean easily reached third . . . and a long-awaited moment.</p><p>“I almost cried,” Dean said. “We kept it inside, though. I’ve been waiting a long time for that. I’m super happy it came at this stadium, with this team and with these guys.</p><p>“I’m going to watch the video a couple of time, feel the moment and get back to it tomorrow.’’</p><p>Dean admitted his path hasn’t been easy, even if he was starting to heat up at Iowa, where he was batting .238 with eight doubles, two triples and three homers and 14 stolen bases in 56 games. He reported for his first game at Wrigley Field on Friday after the Cubs optioned catcher <b>Moises Ballesteros</b>, who was struggling offensively, to their top affiliate.</p><p>“I played baseball my whole life, I like to think I’m a capable hitter,” Dean said. “Whatever the team needs, though.”</p><p>Dean said the Dodgers sent him a World Series ring that arrived in Iowa as he left for Chicago.</p><p>“Just crazy timing,” he said.</p><p>Dean said he just planned to simply stare at the ball he struck for the hit before sending it to his parents for safe keeping. He credited this parents for giving him a “support system” through his travails, even at times when he considered leaving baseball.</p><p>“Baseball is a hard game, No. 1,” he said. “I was in the minor leagues for a while for, 2.”</p><p>Counsell was aware of the significance of Dean’s hit.</p><p>“The big thing is Justin’s been playing this game for a long time,” he said. “It’s a little different when you go though what Justin’s gone through in the game and played the game as long as he had.’’</p><p><b>Hoosier tune-up for Boyd</b></p><p>Opening Day starter <b>Matthew Boyd</b> was in the Cubs’ clubhouse on Friday and finally seems be nearing a return to the Cubs’ depleted rotation.</p><p>Fingers crossed.</p><p>The 35-year-old left-hander will shuttle to Indiana for a rehab start for the High-A South Bend Cubs on Saturday hen they play at Fort Wayne. Counsell hopes Boyd will be ready to rejoin the rotation after the minor-league tune-up.</p><p>Boyd was on track to return at San Francisco last weekend, but that was pushed back after he experienced some shoulder soreness after throwing a bullpen session Tuesday at Colorado.</p><p>Boyd, an All-Star in 2025, has started just five games this season and is 2-1 with a 6.00 ERA. He’s still trying to come back from a second stint on the injured list after his surgery to repair torn meniscus in his left knee. He suffered the freak injury while playing with his kids at home on May 4.</p><p>Boyd missed three weeks in April with a biceps strain. Last season, Boyd was 14-8 with 3.21 ERA in 31 starts.</p><p><b>Ex-Cub farmhand impressing with Jays</b></p><p>Rookie and one-time Cub farmhand <b>Yohendrick Pinango</b> batted cleanup and played left field for the Blue Jays.</p><p>In his first major-league season at age 24, he’s batting .283 through 42 games with four homers and 18 RBI, playing in both left and right.</p><p>The 24-year-old Venezuelan signed with the Cubs as a free agent in June 2018, then was deal to the Blue Jays in July 2024 with <b>Josh Rivera</b> for pitcher <b>Nate Pearson</b>.</p><p>Pinango never advanced above Double-A Tennessee with the Cubs.<br></p>

entries.title: Chicago man wanted for wife's murder returned to the U.S. by FBI
entries.summary:
A man accused of killing wife on their wedding night in 2012 was returned to the Chicago area on Thursday. Arnoldo Jimenez, a fugitive on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list, was arrested in Monterrey, Mexico in January 2025.

Jimenez arrived at O'Hare airport on Thursday afternoon and was transferred to local custody, an FBI Chicago spokesperson said Friday.

“Jimenez was wanted in connection with the murder of Estrella Carrera who was found deceased less than 48 hours after their wedding,” the federal agency's Chicago office had announced Thursday on social media platform X.

The FBI worked with FBI Legat Mexico City, La Agencia de Investigación Criminal-INTERPOL and Burbank Police Department on the case.

FBI Chicago had no details about when Jimenez will appear in Cook County court. Burbank Police Department could not be reached on Friday for comment.

Authorities arrested Jimenez last year in connection with the 2012 slaying of Carrera, his wife. He was wanted for first degree murder and unlawful flight to avoid prosecution, according to an FBI poster.

Jimenez, 44, was last seen after an impromptu wedding reception at a night club in May 2012, the day before the body of Carrera was found in the bathtub of her apartment in southwest suburban Burbank. Carrera, 26, was still in the silver dress she had worn during the wedding ceremony at City Hall.

A warrant for Jimenez’s arrest for first-degree murder was entered a few days later, and he spent nearly 13 years on the run before his arrest.

His name was added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list in 2019, with a reward for information leading to his arrest that over the years rose from $10,000 to $250,000.

FBI Chicago and Burbank Police Department could not be reached on Friday for comment about when Jimenez will appear in court.

Investigators believed Jimenez argued with Carrera after leaving their wedding reception in his black 2006 Maserati. Authorities had theorized Jimenez fatally stabbed the mother of his 2-year-old son in the car, then moved her body into the bathroom of the apartment, the Sun-Times has previously reported..

Family members had called police to check the apartment when Carrera did not turn up to pick up the toddler and her 8-year-old daughter from relatives the day after the wedding.

Authorities said they believed Jimenez fled to central Mexico, where he had family in the state of Durango. Investigators tracked Jimenez’s cellphone for less than a day before it went dark, but in that time they saw that he had moved from the Chicago area to southern Illinois, through Memphis and Arkansas before going dark at Hildalgo, Texas, near the border. Monterrey, where Jimenez was arrested, is about 150 miles from Hildalgo in the Mexican state of Nuevo Leon.

entries.title: Chicago's Black cowboys celebrate Juneteenth with South Side horseback ride
entries.summary: <p>Before leading a group of equestrians on a Juneteenth horseback ride through Chicago’s South Side, Murdock circles them up at Washington Park for a pep talk.</p><p>The 78-year-old horseman, who goes by Murdock — just Murdock, no first name — is president of the Broken Arrow Horseback Riding Club.</p><p>He reminded the group of around 20 riders about the rules of the road. Illinois law allows horseback riding on roads, but not highways. Murdock told them to stay to the right side of the road, be mindful of cars and that they have the right of way. entries.title: Prospect's Nathan Cichy chooses Illinois after previously committing to Harvard
entries.summary: <p>Nathan Cichy’s decision was made and his bags were packed.</p><p>The Prospect receiver was committed to Harvard and was ready to head east after competing in the IHSA boys track state meet.</p><p>But then Illinois came calling.</p><p>After some late comings and goings, the Fighting Illini were looking to add to their receiver room heading into this fall. Cichy flipped his commitment to Illinois in late May and two weeks later he was moving into his dorm room and participating in team meetings.</p><p>“It was definitely a whirlwind,” Cichy told the Sun-Times. “That same week [coach Bret Bielema] offered me, we went down for a visit and there’s a lot going through the mind.”</p><p>Including academics, a big priority for someone with six Ivy League offers who was on the 26-member IHSA Academic All-State team for all sports.</p><p>Illinois’ business school has a 3% acceptance rate, but Cichy made the cut.</p><p>“That’s a huge factor, too,” he said. “The business school is going to be great. I’ll still get into finance, I’ll still make a ton of connections and also get the connections within a Big Ten football program. Because a lot of these guys, they all have the work ethic to become very successful people. And that’s the type of people I want to surround myself with.”</p><p>Cichy’s football credentials are impressive as well. Last fall, the 6-1, 190-pounder caught 50 passes for more than 800 yards with 11 touchdowns to bring his career totals to 142 receptions, 2,213 yards and 28 TDs.</p><p>He won a Class 3A state medal in the 100-meter hurdles last month and also -anchored three Prospect relays at state.</p><p>Now he’s ready to compete for playing time with the Illini.</p><p>“They’re going to put the best guys out there,” he said. “It’s really on me. If I work hard enough and get to that skill [level], I’m going to be playing.”</p><p>Halliman to Illini</p><p>Another local player heading to Illinois, but in the 2027 cycle, is Lincoln-Way East offensive lineman Mason Halliman.</p><p>The state’s No. 18 player in his class in the 247Sports composite rankings had a variety of options with more than 15 Power Four offers, including Michigan, Ole Miss and Tennessee.</p><p>But the Fighting Illini were an easy choice for the 6-5, 280-pounder, whose brother -attended the school.</p><p>“I’ve been around Illinois a large part of my life,” Halliman told the Sun-Times. “I fell in love . . . with the people there and the culture.”</p><p>Since last season, Halliman has been working hard at his craft.</p><p>“I want to polish my footwork and make it the best,” he said. “I’m a smaller offensive lineman in general. Footwork and technique is going to take me a long way.”</p><p>He came to football later than some players.</p><p>“I started playing in seventh grade, but I was hurt that year and didn’t play a full season,” Halliman said. “In eighth grade, I broke my leg. I wasn’t a guy who got injured a lot. Those two injuries came out of nowhere.”</p><p>But since he arrived at Lincoln-Way East, he has been on the rise.</p><p>“It’s moved really fast,” Halliman said. “I was just praying about being recruited and getting an offer. Now I’m living my dream.”<br></p>

Enjoy the beauty of your daily world.</p><h2>Cancer (June 21-July 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> You're chatty and eager to learn the latest gossip and catch up on news. Enjoy shopping for something pretty for yourself and loved ones.</p><h2>Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Today you identify with something you own more than usual. You want to take care of it or admire it. (You certainly don’t want to lend it.) This is actually a good day for you to buy wardrobe items for yourself. You'll also enjoy active and competitive interactions with friends and groups.</p><h2>Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-6f0000" name="html-embed-module-6f0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>dynamic</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Things will tend to go your way today. Why not ask the universe for a favor? After all, you look fabulous because the sun is at the top of your chart casting you in a flattering spotlight. Say yes if you're asked to take on extra responsibilities because you'll shine! (A secret love affair might occur.)</p><h2>Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Conflicting influences exist for you today. In one way, you want to hide and enjoy your own privacy (with good food and drink). However, another influence makes you want to get out there and fly your colors! In fact, you want to travel. It's your call.</p><h2>Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Your emotional contact with friends is important to you today. You might even feel more protective or supportive than usual toward someone. Possibly, this same attitude applies to a group. This is also a good day to examine your overall goals in life. How well are you doing at the art of living?</p><h2>Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> You are noticed today. In fact, some people will know personal details about your private life for some reason. Don’t worry about this. But do remember that you need more sleep right now. Be patient with partners and close friends.</p><h2>Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-6f0000" name="html-embed-module-6f0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>dynamic</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Try to do something different today because you're restless for adventure. Obviously, travel would be an excellent choice. But if you can't travel, then explore your own neighborhood or your city. Meet new people. Learn new information through books, film and talking to others.</p><h2>Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> This is a pleasant time for you, which is why you want to socialize with others and explore fun outings. Relations with partners and friends are also reassuring and supportive. Today, discussions about shared property, taxes or debt might come up. You'll handle this.</p><h2>Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Ideally, you have to go more than halfway when dealing with others to make everything copacetic today. (It's not a big deal.) Home and family are your focus right now. Relations with co-workers are especially rewarding — perhaps even romantic.</p><h2>If today is your birthday</h2><p>Actress Nicole Kidman (1967) shares your birthday today. You're curious, idealistic and can think on your feet. You're also outgoing, exuberant and intuitive. This is a year for wrapping up things and moving on because you are finishing a nine-year cycle. Take inventory of your life. Do some internal and external housecleaning. Commune with nature.</p>
